newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaican leader Manley gravely ill - report.
newsitem.headline: Jamaican leader Manley gravely ill - report.

text.p: Former Jamaican Prime Minister Michael Manley, who has been battling prostate cancer for six years, is gravely ill, according to a newspaper report in the Caribbean nation on Thursday.
The Gleaner quoted an unnamed family member as saying that Manley, 72, was "very, very ill... his general progress seems to be going the wrong way."
The family source told the newspaper that Manley was "nearly bedridden and cannot get up much."

The Caribbean News Agency reported that a release from Prime Minister Percival Patterson's office late on Wednesday had said the Jamaica Cabinet had conveyed Christmas greetings to Manley and expressed best wishes for a speedy recovery.

Manley was a towering figure in Jamaican -- and Caribbean -- politics for decades. The son of Norman Manley, the founder of the People's National Party and himself a former prime minister, he was Jamaica's prime minister and head of the PNP government between 1972 and 1980 and 1989 to 1992.

A charismatic figure known for his advocacy of Third World issues, Manley and his government in the 1970s garnered the hostility of Washington for its alliance with the government of Cuban President Fidel Castro. But he changed his stance and in fact attended a private dinner at the White House where President Bush hailed him as an apostle of free-market economics.
